pages.title: Documentation

pages.text: 212 operations, generated from openapi.yaml. Each page lists the scope, whether it works only from this computer, parameters, request and response fields, error codes, and a curl and Python example. Streams are in asyncapi.yaml; error codes in errors.md. Every call except...
pages.title: API reference: one page per endpoint

pages.text: POST /v1/accounts. Adds the account to the config file the Bridge loaded (or creates the per-user bridge.config.json when it started without one), keeping the file's other content, and starts using it without a restart.
pages.title: Add a broker or paper account (saved to the config file, usable at once)

pages.text: POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/session. Saves the non-secret values (API key, client id, access token) encrypted at rest, then logs in where the broker needs it.
pages.title: Connect or log in to the broker

pages.text: DELETE /v1/accounts/{accountId}/session.
pages.title: Forget the broker session (saved keys stay)

pages.text: GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}.
pages.title: One account

pages.text: GET /v1/accounts. Only accounts this key may use are listed.
pages.title: Your configured accounts and their session state

pages.text: GET /v1/brokers. Capabilities come from each adapter's declared contract; limits from the Bridge's broker policy table (each number marked verified or not).
pages.title: Supported brokers and what each can do

pages.text: DELETE /v1/accounts/{accountId}. For an account added by mistake.
pages.title: Remove an account (from the config file and the running Bridge)

pages.text: POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/test.
pages.title: Make one cheap authenticated broker call

pages.text: POST /mcp. JSON-RPC 2.0 per the Model Context Protocol.
pages.title: MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint for AI assistants

pages.text: POST /v1/backup. This computer only, admin key.
pages.title: Make a backup now

pages.text: GET /v1/backup. This computer only, admin key.
pages.title: The last backup, the schedule and the copies kept on this computer

pages.text: POST /v1/collections. A static collection holds a list of symbols.
pages.title: Create a collection

pages.text: DELETE /v1/collections/{name}. Refused with 409 while a download, recording or rule that is running uses it, unless force=true.
pages.title: Delete a collection

pages.text: POST /v1/collections/{name}/duplicate. Without a name the copy is called -copy (then -copy2 ...).
pages.title: Copy a collection under a new name

pages.text: GET /v1/collections/{name}/estimate. Rows, bytes and broker calls before you start.
pages.title: Size of downloading a collection (symbols x intervals x days)

pages.text: GET /v1/collections/{name}/export. JSON is the definition (a universe stays a universe) and imports back with POST /v1/collections/import.
pages.title: A collection as a CSV or JSON file

pages.text: GET /v1/collections/{name}.
pages.title: One collection with its symbols or universe

pages.text: GET /v1/collections/{name}/usage. The downloads, recordings, auto-record rules and datasets that use it.
pages.title: What is made from this collection

pages.text: POST /v1/collections/import. JSON: a collection ({ name, kind, symbols | universe }), a plain list of symbols (with name in the query), a file that GET /v1/collections/{name}/export wrote, or { collections: [...] }.
pages.title: Make collections from CSV or JSON

pages.text: GET /v1/collections. Summaries without symbol lists, ordered by name.
pages.title: List collections (static lists and option universes)

pages.text: GET /v1/collections/{name}/resolve. A static collection answers its list.
pages.title: The concrete symbols of a collection right now

pages.text: PATCH /v1/collections/{name}. A rename keeps the collection's id and its old name keeps working.
pages.title: Change a collection, or rename it (send `name`)

pages.text: POST /api/v1/analyzer.
pages.title: Analyzer (paper) mode status for this key

pages.text: POST /api/v1/analyzer/toggle.
pages.title: Switch analyzer mode for this key (off needs a live key)

pages.text: POST /api/v1/basketorder.
pages.title: Several orders in one call

pages.text: POST /api/v1/cancelallorder.
pages.title: Cancel every open order

pages.text: POST /api/v1/cancelorder.
pages.title: Cancel an order

pages.text: POST /api/v1/closeposition.
pages.title: Square off every open position

pages.text: POST /api/v1/depth.
pages.title: Market depth

pages.text: POST /api/v1/expiry.
pages.title: Expiry dates

pages.text: POST /api/v1/funds.
pages.title: Funds

pages.text: POST /api/v1/history.
pages.title: Candles

pages.text: POST /api/v1/holdings.
pages.title: Holdings with statistics

pages.text: POST /api/v1/intervals.
pages.title: Supported candle intervals

pages.text: POST /api/v1/margin.
pages.title: Margin calculation (not available yet)

pages.text: POST /api/v1/modifyorder.
pages.title: Modify an open order

pages.text: POST /api/v1/multiquotes.
pages.title: Quotes for up to 200 symbols

pages.text: POST /api/v1/openposition.
pages.title: Net quantity for one symbol and product

pages.text: POST /api/v1/optionchain.
pages.title: Option chain

pages.text: POST /api/v1/optionsorder.
pages.title: Order an option by offset (ATM, ITM2, OTM1 ...)

pages.text: POST /api/v1/optionsymbol.
pages.title: Option symbol for an offset

pages.text: POST /api/v1/orderbook.
pages.title: Order book with statistics

pages.text: POST /api/v1/orderstatus.
pages.title: One order's status

pages.text: POST /api/v1/ping.
pages.title: Check the key and the account the calls act on

pages.text: POST /api/v1/placeorder.
pages.title: Place an order

pages.text: POST /api/v1/placesmartorder.
pages.title: Order towards a target position size

pages.text: POST /api/v1/positionbook.
pages.title: Positions

pages.text: POST /api/v1/quotes.
pages.title: Quote for one symbol

pages.text: POST /api/v1/search.
pages.title: Instrument search

pages.text: POST /api/v1/splitorder.
pages.title: One order split into pieces

pages.text: POST /api/v1/symbol.
pages.title: Instrument details

pages.text: POST /api/v1/tradebook.
pages.title: Trade book

pages.text: POST /v1/downloads/{downloadId}/cancel. Files of items that were already whole are kept; half-written parts are dropped.
pages.title: Cancel a job

pages.text: POST /v1/downloads. Saves candles to files on this computer as a background job.
pages.title: Start a history download, or only estimate it with dryRun=1

pages.text: DELETE /v1/datasets/{name}. This computer only, admin key.
pages.title: Delete a dataset and its files

pages.text: DELETE /v1/downloads/{downloadId}. This computer only, admin key.
pages.title: Delete a job and its files

pages.text: GET /v1/instruments/export. Streams every instrument the connected brokers' masters hold (symbol, exchange, kind, underlying, name, expiry, strike, right, lot size, tick size, freeze quantity, ISIN), optionally for one exchange or kind.
pages.title: The instrument master as a CSV or JSONL file

pages.text: GET /v1/datasets/{name}. Each file lists its coverage (the stretch already fetched and stored) and its gaps (places inside it where bars are missing; a thin stock has no bar for a minute with no trade, so a gap is reported and never filled with a made-up bar).
pages.title: One dataset with its files, coverage and gaps

pages.text: GET /v1/downloads/{downloadId}.
pages.title: One download job with its progress and items

pages.text: GET /v1/downloads/{downloadId}/files/{name}. The file as the Bridge wrote it.
pages.title: Stream one file of a job (or manifest.json)

pages.text: GET /v1/datasets. A dataset is a named set of files (one per symbol and interval) that grows by incremental updates.
pages.title: Datasets stored on this computer

pages.text: GET /v1/downloads/{downloadId}/files.
pages.title: The files of a job, as listed in its manifest

pages.text: GET /v1/downloads. The list leaves out each job's items unless include=items.
pages.title: Download jobs, newest first

pages.text: POST /v1/downloads/{downloadId}/pause. The job keeps what it has written and continues from there when resumed.
pages.title: Pause a queued or running job

pages.text: POST /v1/downloads/{downloadId}/resume.
pages.title: Resume a paused job, or retry the failed items of a failed job

pages.text: POST /v1/datasets/{name}/update. Starts a job that continues every series of the dataset from its last stored bar.
pages.title: Fetch what is new since the last stored bar

pages.text: PATCH /v1/datasets/{name}.
pages.title: Rename a dataset or change its tags and title

pages.text: PATCH /v1/downloads/{downloadId}.
pages.title: Rename a job or change its tags

pages.text: Every error is application/problem+json with code, status, detail, retryable and requestId. The code is stable (codes are added, never renamed); detail is for people. retryable answers one question: is it safe to send exactly this request again? A write whose outcome is unknown...
pages.title: Error codes

pages.text: DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/dead-letters.
pages.title: Forget this subscription's dead letters

pages.text: POST /v1/subscriptions. The target is an outside URL, so this works from this computer only.
pages.title: Send events to a URL, signed (this computer only)

pages.text: DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}.
pages.title: Remove a subscription, its queue, dead letters, log and stored secret

pages.text: GET /v1/events/status.
pages.title: The event log, open connections and the webhook queue

pages.text: GET /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}.
pages.title: One webhook subscription with its health

pages.text: GET /v1/events/topics. A read key sees no admin-only topic.
pages.title: The topics this key may receive

pages.text: GET /v1/events. The same events, filters and cursor as the stream, in one answer.
pages.title: Replay events as JSON (the polling twin of the stream)

pages.text: GET /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/dead-letters.
pages.title: Events that could not be delivered, newest first

pages.text: GET /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/deliveries. Every attempt with its outcome, HTTP status and a short failure code.
pages.title: The delivery log, newest first

pages.text: GET /v1/subscriptions. The URL's path and the signing secret are never returned, only the host.
pages.title: Webhook subscriptions

pages.text: GET /v1/events/ws. ws://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/events/ws?token=&topics=order.*&since=.
pages.title: WebSocket stream of Bridge events (upgrade), same events and cursor as the SSE stream

pages.text: GET /v1/events/stream. GET /v1/events/stream?token=&topics=order.,download.&since=.
pages.title: Server-Sent Events stream of Bridge events, with replay from a cursor

pages.text: POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/dead-letters/{deliveryId}/retry.
pages.title: Put a dead letter back in the queue (this computer only)

pages.text: POST /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/test. One attempt, not queued and not retried; it appears in the delivery log.
pages.title: Send one signed test event now (this computer only)

pages.text: PATCH /v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}. Only the fields sent change.
pages.title: Change a subscription (this computer only)

pages.text: GET /v1/symbols/convert.
pages.title: Convert one symbol between formats

pages.text: POST /v1/symbols/convert.
pages.title: Convert up to 200 symbols in one call

pages.text: GET /v1/instruments/{symbol}.
pages.title: Resolve one instrument (lot size, tick size, freeze quantity)

pages.text: GET /v1/symbols/resolve. Reads what chart tools, spreadsheets and alerts write (NSE:MM, NSEINDEX:NIFTY 50, NSE:RELIANCE-EQ, Reliance) and answers the one instrument it means, how it got there (rule, rules) and the ranked candidates.
pages.title: Resolve a name to one instrument, with the reason

pages.text: GET /v1/instruments/search.
pages.title: Search instruments across connected brokers' masters

pages.text: GET /v1/symbols/validate. For a spreadsheet or an alert author: type a symbol, see the exact canonical form the Bridge will use and its lot size.
pages.title: Check one symbol (canonical form, lot size, tradable)

pages.text: POST /v1/symbols/validate.
pages.title: Check up to 200 symbols in one call

pages.text: POST /v1/keys. The key is in the response once and cannot be shown again; only a scrypt hash is stored.
pages.title: Create an API key

pages.text: GET /v1/keys. An admin key limited to some accounts lists only keys limited to those same accounts.
pages.title: List API keys (never the key itself)

pages.text: DELETE /v1/keys/{keyId}. An admin key limited to some accounts can revoke only keys limited to those accounts; any other key answers 404, as an unknown id does.
pages.title: Revoke a key (takes effect immediately)

pages.text: POST /v1/sign-in. Used by the dashboard when it is opened from mc-bridge start --open or mc-bridge open, whose link carries a one-time code in the URL fragment (/dashboard#signin=, never sent to the server in a URL).
pages.title: Exchange a one-time sign-in code for a dashboard key

pages.text: GET /v1/limits. With explain=1 the report also says why a request may have been slow or refused, in numbers instead of log lines (pools, consumers).
pages.title: Broker limits, safety limits and current budgets per account

pages.text: GET /v1/usage. Per account and endpoint class: the binding window, every window (windows: this second, this minute, today) and today's counters.
pages.title: How much of each budget is used, queued and saved by streaming, caching and coalescing

pages.text: GET /v1/calendar/holidays. From the holiday list shipped with the Bridge (the NSE and BSE circulars; the list's date and source are in calendar).
pages.title: Trading holidays of a year for an exchange

pages.text: GET /v1/calendar/sessions. Whether the date is a trading day and why not when it is not (weekend, holiday), the pre-open, open and close times (IST), a special session such as Muhurat trading, and the neighbouring trading days.
pages.title: The session of one date (trading day or not, and the times)

pages.text: GET /v1/calendar/status. open, pre-open or closed, by the Bridge's clock in IST, with the reason (a holiday is named), when it closes or opens and the next regular or special open.
pages.title: Is the exchange open now, and when does it next open

pages.text: GET /v1/depth.
pages.title: Market depth (5 levels where the broker offers it)

pages.text: GET /v1/expiries. See /v1/reference/expiries for kind, lot and holiday shifts.
pages.title: Expiry dates for an underlying

pages.text: GET /v1/history. Give from+to, or to+countback.
pages.title: Historical candles, automatically split across broker limits

pages.text: GET /v1/ltp.
pages.title: Last traded price for up to 200 symbols

pages.text: GET /v1/optionchain. Works for every F&O stock; see /v1/options/underlyings.
pages.title: Option chain with IV and Greeks

pages.text: GET /v1/quotes.
pages.title: Full quotes for up to 200 symbols

pages.text: POST /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}/chats.
pages.title: Put a chat on the list (alerts, and optionally commands)

pages.text: POST /v1/notify/targets. The token is checked with Telegram (getMe) and stored encrypted in the secrets store.
pages.title: Add a Telegram bot (or replace the token of the same bot)

pages.text: DELETE /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}/chats/{chatKey}.
pages.title: Remove a chat from the list

pages.text: DELETE /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}.
pages.title: Remove a bot and forget its token and chats

pages.text: POST /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}/find-chat. The person sends the bot a message (for example /start); the Bridge reads it and offers the chat to confirm.
pages.title: Find chats that recently wrote to the bot

pages.text: GET /v1/notify/events.
pages.title: Every event with its plain label and whether it is on

pages.text: GET /v1/notify/status. Plain-words state for the dashboard and mc-bridge doctor.
pages.title: Notification health: queue, last delivery, last error per target

pages.text: GET /v1/notify/targets. The bot token and chat ids are never returned: only a token hint, the bot name, a chat name and the last four digits of each chat id.
pages.title: List Telegram bots and their chats (masked)

pages.text: PUT /v1/notify/events. Only the fields sent change.
pages.title: Choose which events are sent, quiet hours and the morning reminder

pages.text: POST /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}/test.
pages.title: Send a test message and report delivery per chat

pages.text: PATCH /v1/notify/targets/{targetId}/chats/{chatKey}.
pages.title: Allow or stop commands from a chat

pages.text: POST /v1/orders/cancel-all.
pages.title: Cancel every open order for an account (or all accounts this key may use)

pages.text: DELETE /v1/orders/{orderId}.
pages.title: Cancel an open order

pages.text: POST /v1/tickets/{ticketId}/confirm. Used by the Bridge's own confirmation page on this computer.
pages.title: Human confirmation of an order prepared by an AI assistant or webhook

pages.text: GET /v1/orders/{orderId}.
pages.title: One order (refreshed from the broker for live orders)

pages.text: GET /v1/orders/by-client-id/{clientOrderId}.
pages.title: Look up an order by your own clientOrderId

pages.text: GET /v1/orders.
pages.title: Orders (newest first)

pages.text: GET /v1/tickets. The dashboard's "Pending confirmations" panel polls this (or listens on the stream) and shows each ticket's full order, its source (AI assistant or webhook) and its checks.
pages.title: Orders waiting for a human confirmation

pages.text: GET /v1/trades.
pages.title: Executions (trade book)

pages.text: PATCH /v1/orders/{orderId}. Counts towards the order-rate cap.
pages.title: Modify an open order

pages.text: POST /v1/orders. Every order passes the safety checks.
pages.title: Place an order (paper unless you ask for live)

pages.text: POST /v1/orders/batch. A convenience for alerts that need two legs (a hedge and a main order), not a strategy engine: the legs do not know about each other and nothing is rolled back.
pages.title: Place up to 20 independent orders in one call

pages.text: POST /v1/orders/to-target. "Be long 3 lots", "be flat", "be short 50 shares", the way a strategy alert says it.
pages.title: Place only the order that gets a position to a target size

pages.text: POST /v1/orders/preview. Resolves the symbol and lot size, runs every safety check, and returns warnings and the estimated value.
pages.title: Check an order without sending it

pages.text: POST /v1/tickets/{ticketId}/reject. The "no" that goes with confirm.
pages.title: A person declines an order prepared by an AI assistant or webhook

pages.text: GET /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}.
pages.title: Paper account summary

pages.text: POST /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}/margin. Portfolio model (server/bridge/calc/span-margin.js): approximate, not the exchange's SPAN.
pages.title: Margin of a basket against the paper book (approximate, nothing is placed)

pages.text: GET /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}/daily. One row per IST day: equity, realised, unrealised, charges, the day's change in equity (pnl), used margin and open positions.
pages.title: Daily P&L snapshots of a paper account, oldest first

pages.text: POST /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}/daily. Marks the book to the latest prices and stores today's row.
pages.title: Take today's P&L snapshot now

pages.text: POST /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}/reset.
pages.title: Clear paper orders and positions and start again

pages.text: POST /v1/paper/accounts/{accountId}/reset/undo. Works for 2 minutes after a reset and only while no order has been placed since.
pages.title: Put back the paper book from before the last reset

pages.text: PUT /v1/pooling/consent. acknowledge must equal the current notice.version.
pages.title: Accept the pooling notice for chosen accounts

pages.text: GET /v1/pooling. Pooling is off until you accept the notice.
pages.title: Whether market-data reads may be spread over your own accounts

pages.text: DELETE /v1/pooling/consent. Each account serves only its own reads again.
pages.title: Withdraw the pooling consent

pages.text: POST /v1/positions/convert. Paper: moves the quantity to the other product at its average price (no order, no fill, no charge); refused into Intraday after the square-off time, while the kill switch is on, when the other product holds the opposite side, or into a product the cont
pages.title: Convert a position between Intraday (MIS) and carry (NRML)

pages.text: GET /v1/funds.
pages.title: Funds and margin for one account

pages.text: GET /v1/holdings.
pages.title: Demat holdings for one account

pages.text: GET /v1/positions.
pages.title: Positions for one account (live from the broker, or paper)

pages.text: POST /v1/margin/basket. What the positions would need together, before anything is placed.
pages.title: Margin for up to 50 prospective positions (read only)

pages.text: DELETE /v1/quotas/{keyId}. The key goes back to the quota from the configuration, or the default for its client kind.
pages.title: Remove a key's override

pages.text: GET /v1/quotas. Every key has a request quota (a token bucket) and a weight in the fair queue, so one runaway spreadsheet cannot starve an AI assistant.
pages.title: Each API key's share of the Bridge

pages.text: PUT /v1/quotas/{keyId}. Only the fields you send change.
pages.title: Override one key's quota or weight

pages.text: POST /v1/readiness/check. Runs the checks at once for one account (or every account this key may see).
pages.title: Re-check now (probe and egress lookup, each with a 30 s cooldown)

pages.text: POST /v1/demo/readiness. Exists only when the Bridge runs in demo mode.
pages.title: Demo mode only - simulate a readiness failure on the demo account (restores itself after 10 minutes)

pages.text: GET /v1/readiness. One state per account (ready, warn, cannottrade, paperonly, unknown) with plain-English reasons and the facts each check used.
pages.title: Trading readiness of each live account (cached; no broker call)

pages.text: GET /v1/readiness/history.
pages.title: Recent readiness transitions (newest first)

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings/presets/{presetId}/apply. Applying a preset again does not duplicate its rule (answers 200).
pages.title: Create the preset's rule and turn auto-record on

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings. Real-time class only: a dataClass other than realtime is refused, and a delayed or end-of-day answer is never written.
pages.title: Start a recording of quotes or an option chain

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings/rules. For example: every trading day, record NIFTY and BANKNIFTY option chains, ATM +/- 10, current weekly expiry, every 30 seconds, during market hours.
pages.title: Add an auto-record rule

pages.text: DELETE /v1/recordings/{recordingId}. A recording that belongs to a rule is deleted by deleting the rule (409 otherwise).
pages.title: Delete a recording and its files

pages.text: DELETE /v1/recordings/rules/{ruleId}.
pages.title: Delete a rule (its files stay unless deleteFiles=true)

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}. gaps lists stretches with no data and why (feed silent, login missing, Bridge stopped, budget in use, disk limit).
pages.title: One recording: counters, gaps, disk use, files summary

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/auto.
pages.title: Whether auto-record is on

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/files/{name}. Only names from the file list open.
pages.title: Download one day file as it is on disk

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/rules/{ruleId}.
pages.title: One rule with today's state

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/status. For example: Recording today: 3 rules, 41 symbols, 18 MB, last write 09:31:02.
pages.title: One plain line about today's recording, and the numbers behind it

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/files. One file per symbol per IST trading day, named YYYY-MM-DDEXCHANGESYMBOL.csv (or .jsonl; .gz after compression).
pages.title: The day files of a recording

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/presets. Record index option chains, and Record my watchlist.
pages.title: The one-click presets

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings/rules. Rules from this computer's data folder and from recorder.autoRecord.rules in the config file (source config, read-only here).
pages.title: The auto-record rules

pages.text: GET /v1/recordings. A recording saves this Bridge's own real-time data going forward, because brokers give no history for option chains, open interest snapshots or ticks.
pages.title: List recordings (meta.status is a plain status line)

pages.text: PATCH /v1/recordings/rules/{ruleId}. Only the fields sent change.
pages.title: Change a rule

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/pause.
pages.title: Pause a recording

pages.text: PUT /v1/recordings/auto. Off until a person turns it on.
pages.title: Turn auto-record on or off

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/resume.
pages.title: Resume a paused recording

pages.text: POST /v1/recordings/{recordingId}/stop. A recording that belongs to a rule is changed through the rule (409 otherwise).
pages.title: Stop a recording (final; the files stay)

pages.text: POST /v1/safety/kill-switch. Any key may stop trading; an empty body works (reason "manual").
pages.title: Stop all orders now (any key may do this)

pages.text: GET /v1/safety.

pages.text: GET /v1/sources. Every place the Bridge can read market data from: your broker accounts (kind: broker, always first for real-time data), the built-in free providers, and plugins you granted.

pages.text: PATCH /v1/sources/{id}. enabled: true turns a source on.
pages.title: Turn a source on or off

pages.text: PATCH /v1/sources/settings. autoFallback: true lets a read that no broker account can answer go to a source you turned on, without the read asking for backup=true.

pages.text: GET /xl/history.

pages.text: GET /xl/instrument. One symbol with one field and no format gives a bare value (text/plain, #N/A on error) for a single cell.

pages.text: GET /xl/orders. Columns are fixed - account, mode, orderid, clientorderid, symbol, side, product, ordertype, qty, filledqty, avgprice, price, triggerprice, status, statusmessage, placedat, updatedat (IST), then asof, ages, class, source, stale, error.

pages.text: GET /v1/stream. Connect with ws://127.0.0.1:4300/v1/stream?token= (or an Authorization header from scripts).
